fixtureServer.note: The four requiresOnlineGame scenes cannot be captured without these server-side fixtures, and the fixtures live in a different repository on a personal fork - an upstream crystalserver clone has never had them. This block is the pin. renderer_scenes.py validate enforces three things against it: the vendored copy under vendoredCopy matches the recorded sha256 digests, the anchors agree with FIXTURE_ANCHORS in modules/dev_renderer_baseline/dev_renderer_baseline.lua, and every online scene names an anchor that exists here. Startup events fire only on the GAME_STATE_INIT transition, so installing the scripts into a running server does nothing - it must be restarted.

scenes.toleranceReason: The scene deliberately includes creatures, and a creature on a live server cannot be perfectly frozen from the client: setAnimate stops a thing advancing but leaves it on whatever phase it already held. Consecutive runs measure 16 to 765 differing pixels, roughly one 32x32 sprite, so the limit is raised from the 0.001 default to cover one creature. Anything larger is a real change.

scenes.characterGroupReason: ProtocolGame forces world light and every creature light to 255/215 for any player whose group carries hasfulllight (groups 4-7), and LightView sets m_isDark = intensity < 250, so the entire LIGHT pool is skipped for such a character. This scene must be captured by a group-1 character or it renders no lights at all.

scenes.ciGateReason: Renders outfit, mount and addon previews from data/things/*, which is gitignored. A CI runner has no game assets, so this scene captures an empty preview there; gating it would freeze a blank image as the accepted reference. Captured and archived as an artifact only.

Renders creature, item, effect and missile widget previews from data/things/*, which is gitignored. A CI runner has no game assets, so this scene captures empty previews there; gating it would freeze a blank image as the accepted reference. Captured and archived as an artifact only.

scenes.renderPathToleranceReason: The only scene where the two render paths are MEANT to differ. UIGraph's lines are GL_LINE_STRIP with glLineWidth and GL_LINE_SMOOTH on the legacy path, and quads triangulated at record time on the compiled one, because Metal has neither wide nor smoothed lines. Both draw the same vertices at the same widths in the same colours; only the edge pixels differ. Measured on XQuartz at 7,660 differing pixels of 656,880 (1.17%), max channel delta 235. The limit is 0.03 rather than something just above 1.17% because llvmpipe antialiases wide lines where XQuartz rasterises them hard - the same disagreement this scene already carries a cross-environment caveat for in known-deviations.md - so CI was expected to measure more than a local run, and does: 8,734 px (1.33%), max channel delta 168, run 32452811177. Both environments sit comfortably inside the limit, and a structural regression such as a series not drawn at all moves well past 3%.

scenes.note: The sixteen fragment cells plus one unshaded control cell, laid out on rows 0-2 of the shared shader grid. Every cell draws data/images/background_crystal1, which is tracked, so this scene renders identically with or without game assets and is CI-gated. The six outfit cells that used to occupy row 3 are now shader-matrix-outfits. One cell renders differently by environment and the gate cannot cover it: forge_result_silhouette is registered by game_exaltationforge's onLoad, which does not come up without game assets. With assets the cell draws the shader's black silhouette; without them the shader is simply unregistered and the cell draws the unshaded image, logged as 'shader unavailable in this environment'. Both are deterministic, so the llvmpipe reference freezes the unshaded form and the gate holds - but that shader itself is only exercised locally, and a local-versus-llvmpipe comparison of this scene will always differ in that one cell.

scenes.ciGateReason: Renders UICreature previews from data/things/*, which is gitignored, so a CI runner draws them empty; gating it would freeze a blank image as the accepted reference. Split out of shader-matrix on 2026-08-20 precisely so the sixteen fragment cells could be gated without this dependency. Captured and archived as an artifact only.
scenes.note: Outfit - Outline is the only shader in the registry declaring useFramebuffer, so this scene is the only automated coverage of a shader applied at an offscreen blit. It shares the shader grid with shader-matrix, occupying row 0.

scenes.toleranceReason: Captures the same fixture platform as map-core and inherits the same residual: a creature on a live server cannot be perfectly frozen from the client. Consecutive runs measured 778 differing pixels, roughly one sprite.
scenes.multiCapture: One capture per map shader plus a Default frame to diff against: shader-matrix-map-01-default.png through shader-matrix-map-14-noise.png. A map shader applies to the whole composed map, so only one can be shown per frame.
scenes.note: Covers what shader-matrix structurally cannot: map shaders bind at the MAP framebuffer to screen blit through the pool's onBeforeDraw hook, which also writes the four map uniforms, and Client::canDraw(MAP) is g_game.isOnline(), so none of it is reachable offline.

scenes.ciCaptureReason: Needs things a headless runner cannot provide. modules/startup/startup.lua sets a desktop minimum window size of exactly the capture size, so resize can only be tested by growing, and a headless X server is created at exactly that size. There is also no window manager, so setFullscreen is silently dropped while the client still flips its own state bit, making isFullscreen a false-positive assertion. The scene also emits several files rather than one <id>.png.

scenes.characterGroupReason: Deliberately the inverse of lighting-overlap: a hasfulllight character pins world light to 255, which disables the LIGHT pool and makes the surface platform immune to the day/night cycle this build seeds from the wall clock.
